prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim. Injury: neck strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1438; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following report of a collision at an intersection. Insured vehicle was turning left when it was struck by an oncoming vehicle that was proceeding straight through. Police report requested. No citation information available yet.

Entry 2: Spoke with claimant by phone. Claimant reports neck pain and stiffness beginning shortly after the impact. Claimant is not represented by an attorney and states they are handling the matter directly. Claimant has agreed to provide medical records once received.

Entry 3: Reviewed photos submitted by insured. Visible damage to driver side front quarter panel and headlight assembly. Vehicle drivable but towed from scene as a precaution. Repair estimate requested from preferred shop.

Entry 4: Claimant seen by treating provider for neck strain. Diagnosis noted as cervical strain with recommendation for rest, over-the-counter pain relief, and follow-up in two weeks. No fracture or neurological findings reported. Records received and added to file.

Entry 5: Liability assessment completed. Based on the statement of both drivers and the independent witness account, the adjuster finds the insured driver primarily responsible for failing to yield during the left turn. Claim moved to settlement review. Claimant to be contacted with a written offer after the medical file is confirmed as complete.
